title: Resolved engineering brief - NaCl evaporation batch plant
narrative:
This brief consolidates the Stage 1 notes for the NaCl evaporation laboratory plant. The system is a staged batch process with discrete controller sequencing, liquid transfer between vessels, evaporation in B5, condensation in K1/B6, cooling in B6 and B7, and return pumping back to the charging vessels. Canonical equipment names are B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, K1, B6, B7, P1, P2, V1, V3, V5, V6, V8, V9, V11, V12, V15, V18, V20, V22, V23, V24, V25, central controller, M-301 agitator, and instruments LIS-301, QI-302, LIS-501, QIS-502, TIS-602, TIS-702, FIS-801, LIS-601, LIS-701, PIS-901, PIS-1001, TI-503. Aliases supported by the notes: B1 Charging tank, B2 Charging tank, B3 Mixing tank, B4 Buffer tank, B5 Evaporator vessel, B6 Cooling tank, B7 Cooling tank, K1 Condenser, P1/P2 Return pump, controller.sensors for the sensor bundle, controller.actuators for the actuator bundle, controller.sensors.QIS_502 for QIS-502, and controller.actuators.T5_Heater/T5_Heater/B5_Heater for the B5 heater command. The requirement notes and test procedure establish 15 automated valves as controller outputs: V1, V3, V5, V6, V8, V9, V11, V12, V15, V18, V20, V22, V23, V24, V25. Manual valves V13, V17, V26, V27, and V29 appear only as service or manual alignment items and are not automated process valves.

Physical and logical topology resolved from the engineering register, requirements, diagram, legacy notes, and CR-017 correspondence is as follows. B1 bottom port connects through V8 to the top port of B3. B2 bottom port connects through V9 to the top port of B3. B3 bottom port connects through V11 to the top port of B4. B4 bottom port connects through V12 to the feed port of B5. B5 vapor/condensate port connects to the process side of K1. K1 condensate outlet connects to the top port of B6. B5 concentrate outlet connects through V15 to the top port of B7. B6 bottom port connects to P2 suction, and P2 discharges to B1 through the B1 return valve group. B7 bottom port connects to P1 suction, and P1 discharges to B2 through the B2 return valve group. The approved CR-017 routing resolves the legacy cross-routing text: recovered condensate from B6 returns to B1 via P2, and cooled concentrate from B7 returns to B2 via P1. The older routing text that mapped the B7/P1 branch to B1 and the B6/P2 branch to B2 is superseded. The diagram and datasheet also establish cross-connected bottom return headers/manifolds, but the exact full manifold path beyond the approved valve groups is not completely readable in the notes; therefore only the approved branch destinations and observed commanded valves are taken as resolved routing behavior.

The plant purpose, from the requirement specification and engineering register, is to prepare a mixed water/NaCl batch in B3, transfer it via B4 into evaporator B5, concentrate it in B5, split after evaporation into concurrent condensate and concentrate finishing branches, cool B6 and B7, return condensate to B1 and concentrate to B2, then reset only after both branches complete and time exceeds 2500 s. The acceptance simulation must demonstrate at least one full charge-mix-buffer-evaporate-cool-return cycle, including the controller parallel split and join after evaporation, and must continue beyond 2500 s to demonstrate cycle reset.

Geometry and nominal vessel data from the engineering register are: B1 area 0.07 m^2, height 0.6 m, max level 0.5 m, port level note 0.12 m, initial NaCl mass fraction 0.000. B2 area 0.07 m^2, height 0.6 m, max level 0.5 m, port level note 0.12 m, initial NaCl mass fraction 0.250. B3 area 0.05 m^2, height 0.45 m, max level 0.38 m, port level note 0.1 m, water prefill level 0.13 m current, target NaCl mass fraction after mixing 0.080 kg/kg current, nearly-empty threshold 0.01 m current. B4 area 0.055 m^2, height 0.45 m, max level 0.4 m, port level note 0.1 m. B5 area 0.06 m^2, height 0.45 m, max level 0.4 m, port level note 0.12 m, idle threshold 0.01 m current, batch fill level 0.18 m current, target NaCl mass fraction after evaporation 0.180 kg/kg current, heater duty 20000 W current/approved, heater inhibit level 0.05 m approved. B6 area 0.05 m^2, height 0.4 m, max level 0.35 m, port level note 0.1 m, cooling complete temperature 20 degC current, nominal cooling duty -6500 W current. B7 area 0.05 m^2, height 0.4 m, max level 0.35 m, port level note 0.1 m, cooling complete temperature 25 degC current, nominal cooling duty -4500 W current. One engineering-register row also marks B7 cooling complete temperature 20 degC as superseded, and the CR-017 correspondence confirms the approved/current value is 25 degC.

Layout coordinates dataset provides approximate elevations for gravity pressure-drop implementation. Coordinate system origin is south-west floor datum with z positive up. Equipment base elevations are B1 4.8 m, B2 4.8 m, B3 3.5 m, B4 2.6 m, B5 1.5 m, K1 2.8 m, B6 1.5 m, B7 0.7 m, P1 0.0 m, P2 0.0 m. The requirement specification, engineering register, and layout dataset agree that non-horizontal pipes shall include gravity pressure drop based on relative elevation. Because only equipment base elevations are supplied, later modeling stages may use relative elevation differences grounded in these coordinates; detailed line routing elevations are not available in the notes.

Valve and pump actuation data are grounded as follows. All automated process valves are Boolean discrete open/closed actuators and fail closed on loss of actuator power. Datasheet nominal opening time is 0.7 s and nominal closing time is 0.5 s for the automated valve family, with closed leakage <0.02% Kv and permitted medium temperature range 0-120 degC. These are component datasheet values, not explicit acceptance criteria. P1 and P2 nominal mass flow are 0.30 kg/s and nominal differential pressure 1.8 bar. Both pumps have minimum source level permissive threshold 0.02 m and low discharge pressure alarm threshold 0.8 bar. Relationships tie P1 source level permissive to LIS-701 >0.02 m and low discharge pressure alarm to PIS-901 <0.8 bar; P2 source level permissive to LIS-601 >0.02 m and low discharge pressure alarm to PIS-1001 <0.8 bar.

Controller inputs explicitly required are LIS-301, QI-302, LIS-501, QIS-502, TIS-602, TIS-702, and FIS-801. Additional notes also reference LIS-601, LIS-701, PIS-901, and PIS-1001 for pump permissives and alarms. Controller outputs explicitly required are the 15 automated valve commands, P1, P2, B5 heater, B6 cooler, and B7 cooler. The central controller commands discrete on/off valves. Design review and design note both state automated valves are discrete and fail closed, not modulating.

Medium/modeling configuration is resolved as two distinct contexts. For baseline integration test purposes, Modelica.Media.Water.StandardWater is the required medium for topology and control-sequence validation. For the intended physical plant model, the medium is a water-NaCl mixture with composition-dependent density rho(T,p,w), enthalpy h(T,p,w), heat capacity cp(T,w), saturation pressure p_sat(T,w), and viscosity eta(T,w). The WaterNaCl hierarchy intended in the design note is PartialMedium -> PartialMixtureMedium -> PartialMixtureTwoPhaseMedium -> WaterNaCl. The WaterNaCl implementation must document the known unresolved pump-start convergence issue separately from plant functional requirements. Lab notes record that WaterNaCl still behaves poorly when a pump transition becomes active, that hysteresis removed tiny solver steps around port-level crossing, and that a Q_up fix stopped B5 boil/no-boil switching; these are observations about past modeling behavior, not requirements.

Physical relationships explicitly available from the medium/tank modeling note are: medium pressure equals p_ambient; vessel volume V = area*level + V0; mass m = V*medium.d; species mass vector mXi = m*medium.Xi; internal energy U = m*medium.u; total mass balance der(m) = sum(topPorts.m_flow) + sum(ports.m_flow); internal-energy balance der(U) = sum(H_flow) - p_ambient*der(V). The heater command relation for B5 is HeatB5.Q_flow = if controller.actuators.T5_Heater then 20000 else 0. The condenser-side evaporation/condensation note states: if Q_up > heatPort.Q_flow then m_con = 0; else m_con = -(heatPort.Q_flow - Q_up)/(hv - hl + Xi[1]*(cp*dT_dX + dhl_dX)). Units are not fully established in the notes for hv, hl, Xi[1], dT_dX, and dhl_dX, so later stages must preserve this relation as evidence-grounded but should verify unit consistency when implementing. The viscosity correlation is eta(T,w) = exp(c1*T^3 + c2*T^2 + c3*T + c4 + c5*w + c6*w^2 + c7*w^3) with coefficients c1=-6.83241E-07, c2=0.000765676, c3=-0.297018665, c4=-0.299730079, c5=2.065267182, c6=1.546491257, c7=31.57571595. Some source correlations intentionally omit coefficients; no missing coefficients may be invented.

B5 and K1 must remain distinct physical components in the system architecture even if a combined simulation abstraction is used. The requirement specification allows an evaporator/condenser combined simulation component provided K1 remains identifiable. The medium/modeling note adds that K1 is physically separate from the B5 evaporator model and that the B5 evaporator model exports condensate through an additional fluid port. Lab notebook notes and the requirement specification together support the interpretation that combining B5 and K1 is a simulation abstraction only.

Modeling implementation constraints established by requirement notes and review notes are: insert small junction volumes wherever multiple pressure-drop-only valve/pipe elements can be isolated simultaneously; use the regularized asymmetric loss-factor approach with hysteresis as the default implementation for tank ports that can cross the liquid level; and include static head/gravity pressure drop in non-horizontal pipes based on relative elevation. Tank connections can pass above or below the liquid level. Small junction volumes are specifically to avoid undefined pressure, enthalpy, or composition states when multiple isolating components can simultaneously close.

The control sequence is discrete and staged, with a split into two concurrent regions after evaporation and a join before restart. Because the design note behavior bullets appear to state completion conditions in the same sentence as actuator outputs, they are interpreted together with the engineering-register state-sequence sheet and dataset. The resolved sequence is: Initial: all automated valves closed; P1, P2, B5 heater, B6 cooler, and B7 cooler off. Transition from Initial occurs when startEnable and B3 available, but those exact signals are not defined elsewhere in the notes. Step1: open V8 to transfer B1 liquid to B3 until LIS-301 >= 0.13 m. Step2: after the B1 fill portion, open V9 and continue charging B3 until QI-302 >= 0.080 kg/kg. Step3: open V11 to transfer the mixed batch from B3 to B4 until LIS-301 < 0.01 m. Step4: wait for B5 to be idle; the requirement definition of idle is LIS-501 <0.01 m and V15 closed. The process requirement note also states: when B5 is idle, open V12, B4 to B5. State sequence sheet gives Step4 transition to Step5 when LIS-501 <0.01 m AND NOT V15. Step5: open V12 to transfer B4 contents to B5 until LIS-501 >= 0.18 m. Step6: enable B5 heating at 20000 W when heater permissives are satisfied; continue evaporation until QIS-502 >= 0.180 kg/kg. Heater permissives are LIS-501 >= 0.05 m and FIS-801 >= 0.10 kg/s; heater is inhibited below either threshold. After Step6 completion, sequence splits into two concurrent branches.

Parallel branch A, condensate side: Step12: cool B6 until TIS-602 <= 20 degC. Step13: return recovered condensate from B6 to B1 using P2 and the B1 return valve group, with P2 inhibited unless LIS-601 >0.02 m. The older explicit valve list for this branch in the engineering register is superseded, but the dataset shows observed commands V20, V24, V25, V1, and V3 when P2 runs. Step13 completes when the B6 return branch is complete; a separate state-sequence bullet gives Step7 transitions to Step8 when LIS-701 <0.01 m, but that reference belongs to the other branch as written in the notes and is preserved as an ambiguity below rather than re-assigned.

Parallel branch B, concentrate side: Step8: open V15 to transfer concentrate from B5 to B7 until LIS-501 <0.01 m according to the state-sequence Step8 transition to Step9 when LIS-501 <0.01 m. A preceding Step7 exists in the state-sequence and design note with no transfer actuator and condition involving LIS-701 <0.01 m; the exact role of Step7 is not fully resolved from the notes. Step9: cool B7 until TIS-702 <= 25 degC. Step10/11: return cooled concentrate from B7 to B2 using P1 and the B2 return valve group, with P1 inhibited unless LIS-701 >0.02 m. The older explicit valve list for this branch in the engineering register is superseded, but the dataset shows observed commands V18, V23, V22, V5, and V6 when P1 runs. Join/JoinWait: the split rejoins only when both branches report completion; cycle reset cannot occur until both branches complete and time >2500 s. Join transitions to Initial when A complete AND B complete AND time>2500 s. The dataset shows a JoinWait state at t=2250 s with commands off, and the cycle restarts at t=2505 s.

The operator runbook supplies qualitative expected trends during an acceptance run: B3 level rises during water and brine charge then falls during V11 transfer; B3 concentration changes primarily during V9 brine addition then remains approximately constant until discharge; B5 temperature rises during heating then plateaus near a composition-dependent boiling temperature; B5 concentration rises during evaporation until target is reached; B6 level rises as condensate is produced then later falls during return pumping; B7 level rises when V15 transfers concentrate then later falls during return pumping. These are descriptive behaviors, not acceptance expressions unless tied to explicit quantitative thresholds elsewhere.

Reported variables for later stages, declared here as the output contract, are: time_s [s] simulation time; controller_state [1] controller state encoded for reporting; region [1] active controller region encoded for reporting; B3_level [m] liquid level in B3; B4_level [m] liquid level in B4; B5_level [m] liquid level in B5; B6_level [m] liquid level in B6; B7_level [m] liquid level in B7; B3_X_NaCl [kg/kg] NaCl mass fraction in B3 corresponding to QI-302; B5_X_NaCl [kg/kg] NaCl mass fraction in B5 corresponding to QIS-502; B5_T [degC] B5 temperature corresponding to TI-503 when available as tank temperature; B6_T [degC] B6 temperature corresponding to TIS-602; B7_T [degC] B7 temperature corresponding to TIS-702; FIS801_flow [kg/s] condenser cooling-water flow proof; P1_cmd [1] pump P1 command; P2_cmd [1] pump P2 command; B5_heater_cmd [1] B5 heater command; B6_cooler_cmd [1] B6 cooler command; B7_cooler_cmd [1] B7 cooler command; V1_open [1], V3_open [1], V5_open [1], V6_open [1], V8_open [1], V9_open [1], V11_open [1], V12_open [1], V15_open [1], V18_open [1], V20_open [1], V22_open [1], V23_open [1], V24_open [1], V25_open [1] as the 15 automated valve command signals. The BAT-09 test procedure requires logging state/region, all tank levels, QI-302, QIS-502, TI-503, TIS-602, TIS-702, FIS-801, P1/P2, heater/cooler commands, and all 15 automated valve commands at 5 s or faster.

Simulation horizon is resolved to 3000 s because the dataset records a 3000 s run that demonstrates a full split, join, and restart beyond 2500 s, and the requirement/test notes require continuation beyond 2500 s. No explicit solver tolerance is stated in the notes. A 5 s logging requirement is stated; with a 3000 s run this supports 600 intervals for reported outputs.

Acceptance behavior that can be mechanically checked from the declared variables is: B3 target level reach during Step1; B3 NaCl target reach during Step2; B3 empty threshold during transfer out; B5 fill level reach during Step5; B5 NaCl target reach during Step6; B6 cooling target reach before/with return; B7 cooling target reach before/with return; both P2 and P1 return commands occurring at least once; the approved routing valve groups being energized during the observed return actions; heater permissive logic; and restart only after time >2500 s. The requirement that cycle reset waits for both branches is explicit, but without a directly reported branch-complete variable it is represented in narrative and partly evidenced by the occurrence of both return commands before the restart. No note provides a numeric requirement for exact temperatures, levels, or compositions at final time, so stage targets are checked as ever conditions rather than final conditions.

Resolved conflicts: CR-017-approved return routing replaces the legacy branch mapping; B7 cooling completion target is 25 degC current/approved, replacing archived/proposed 20 degC; baseline StandardWater use is limited to topology/control integration, while WaterNaCl remains the intended physical medium. Open ambiguities remain around the exact semantics of Step7 and the undefined startEnable/B3 available signals, because the notes mention them without enough detail to model them uniquely.
